Both roles cold (RoleLastUsed 2026-06-01 and 2026-08-14), so INERT. The general lesson: a dead grant is a symptom, and the reference census a least-privilege act already requires is also the cheapest available audit of whether a pipeline still works.

compiler_tools.tool: safe-apply.sh HALT-gate and the LGIC naming limb
compiler_tools.note: Recorded as INSTRUMENT failures, not verdicts. The HALT-gate refused with unknown-base because my sparse cone held no agent home folder matching my serial, and its own message is the argument for failing closed: scanning a nonexistent inbox would PASS while a real [STOP] sat unread. The naming limb then BLOCKED on an absent lib/opal_naming.py. Both were fixed by widening the cone -- never by writing a different serial to make a gate pass, which the gate explicitly warns against.

Its own doctrine disqualifies it here: it models (action) and never (action, resource), so it cannot distinguish a grant on a live bucket from one on a 404 -- which is this entire order. The account-wide authorization parse plus per-document read-backs is the instrument that can. The HUD advised it mid-session for the TF-vs-live reconcile; that is a different question from the one these acts answer.
